Sentra Raises $150 Million for Agentic Data Security as Enterprise AI Adoption Accelerates
summary:
Sentra, the agentic data security company, today announced that Capital One Ventures has led a strategic capital investment of $150 million in the company, joining existing investors Bessemer Venture Partners, Zeev Ventures, Standard Investments, Munich Re Ventures and Key1 Capital. As part of the investment, a Capital One representative will join Sentra’s board of directors. The investment follows a year of more than 300% year-over-year growth, as enterprises turn to Sentra to understand their data, control which identities, human and AI, can access it, and keep it governed and protected for AI and autonomous agents.
Your data has a new kind of consumer
Data security was built for people. Three forces have changed that at the same time:
The business wants AI now. Copilots, assistants and cloud AI services are rolling out faster than governance can keep up, leaving security teams balancing business speed with data visibility and governance.
The data explosion. Sensitive data is spread across cloud, SaaS and on-prem, outpacing legacy visibility tools and fragmenting visibility into where sensitive records live or who and what can reach it. Without continuous governance, sensitive information can quickly become over permissioned and overexposed.
AI agents are scaling exponentially. Each agent is a new identity, accessing data continuously and at machine speed, with no central control plane. Large organizations that ran a handful of agents a year ago are on track to run exponentially more within a few years, yet only a small minority say they have the governance in place to control what those agents can access.
“AI agents are now the busiest consumers of enterprise data, and many of them inherit access to data that hasn't been fully classified or governed,” said Yoav Regev, co-founder and CEO of Sentra. “Traditional perimeter controls weren't built for agents moving at machine speed. What organizations can do is make sure the data those agents reach is already secured. Sentra protects data where it lives and controls which identities, human and AI, can reach it, so organizations can deploy AI more quickly while staying in control. This investment lets us bring agentic data security to every enterprise putting agents to work.”
Agentic data security starts with data at rest
Rather than trying to inspect every agent request as it happens, Sentra protects data at rest, where it lives, across cloud, SaaS, data warehouses, on-prem file shares and the knowledge stores AI draws from. By governing the data and access agents depend on ahead of time, Sentra maintains continuous protection beyond traditional perimeters.
Before: Sentra minimizes the exposure footprint. It finds and classifies sensitive data across environments, and maps what people, service accounts and AI agents can reach, including inherited access. It enforces least privilege for non-human identities and removes redundant, obsolete and high-risk data agents should never find.
During: Sentra helps contain an agent fast. Data-aware detection flags unusual access to sensitive data, and automated remediation revokes access and removes risky sharing, routing high-risk issues to data owners and existing workflows.
After: Sentra shows what an agent could have reached, with business context for the datasets involved, giving security, legal and compliance teams the evidence to respond quickly and defensibly.
Where Sentra is investing next
The funding accelerates Sentra’s innovation in agentic data security: broad visibility into agents, copilots and models and the sensitive data they touch, continuous least privilege for human and non-human identities, protection of data at rest before agents reach it, and rapid containment when an agent behaves unexpectedly.
Sentra will also expand its go-to-market by scaling its field and channel programs, growing its brand and marketing, and entering new geographies.
Why enterprises choose Sentra
AI agents now act on enterprise data at machine speed, so security has to understand both the data and who, or what, can access it. Sentra uniquely unifies the two, especially in large, complex environments where other tools fall short. It finds sensitive data and classifies it in ways that fit each business. It also maps every identity, human and non-human, including AI agents, along with the sensitive data each one can access. This lets enterprises govern who has access to what, and fix risky access before agents or attackers exploit it.
Sentra does this without moving the data. It analyzes data where it lives, entirely inside the customer’s environment, so sensitive data never leaves it. Alternatives that copy customer data into their own environment create a separate data estate to secure, adding retention, residency and compliance risks for regulated industries. Leaving data in place also lets Sentra scale efficiently across clouds, SaaS, data warehouses and on-prem systems, with broader coverage at a cost advantage. Customers consistently rate Sentra among the highest in data security posture management on independent peer review platforms.
Chaim Sanders, CISO at Lyft, adopted Sentra as the data security solution to support the organization’s growth. According to Sanders: “Our teams at Lyft want to move fast with AI, but we need to know what data our agents can reach before we turn them on. Sentra gives us that answer across our whole environment, so security helps the rollout instead of slowing it down”.

Veriff Introduces Presence Verification to Detect Deepfakes and Coercion
summary:
Veriff, an enterprise identity verification platform, today launched Presence Verification, a product capability designed to answer one of digital trust’s most pressing questions: Is there actually a real, present, freely participating human on the other side of this interaction?
For years, liveness detection has answered one question: is this a real face, or a photo, mask, or replayed video? That question still matters, but on its own, it no longer tells a business whether it can trust a session. A real face can belong to someone reading from a script or following instructions from a bad actor.
This product evolution comes as businesses confront a new reality online. For the first time, more than half of all web traffic is now estimated to be non-human. At the same time, generative AI has lowered the barrier to creating and executing convincing deepfakes and injection attacks. Businesses must now separate real humans from bots running scripted attacks, protect vulnerable users from coached verification attempts, and crucially, confirm that an authorised, accountable person is directing the AI agents operating on their behalf. For marketplaces, fintechs, and other high-trust platforms, proving human presence at sign-up and at sensitive moments throughout the user journey has become a trust and safety imperative.
How the product works
Presence Verification provides multi-layered defence, analysing over 1,000 risk signals into a single, automated decision:
Liveness and deepfake detection: Identifies spoofing attempts, including screen replays, printouts, 3D masks, mirror selfies, and digitally altered or synthetic media that is injected into the session.
Coercion detection: Analyses full-session video and audio streams for signs of third-party coaching, off-camera influence, or forced compliance and is available across 98 languages.
The Veriff Network: Uses data crosslinking across sessions globally to flag known fraud patterns and repeat offenders, bots, bot farms, and emulated or simulated devices.
A context-aware decision engine: Combines audio and video analysis with emulated or simulated device detection and over a thousand risk signals into one explainable result.
Presence Verification integrates through Veriff’s iOS and Android SDKs. Customers initiate a session via REST API, end-users record a short selfie video in the customer’s app, and Veriff returns an automated decision via webhook. Backed by comprehensive API documentation, drop-in SDK components, and hands-on configuration support from Veriff Solutions Engineers, it is easy to move from sandbox to production with minimal engineering overhead.
Presence Verification significantly improves deepfake detection and detects coercion with more than 98% accuracy. Presence Verification keeps friction low, with funnel conversion above 90%.
“Anything can be automated now. Anyone can be deepfaked or coached by a bad actor. Businesses need to be able to determine whether a real human is present and engaging on their own,” said Rob Brazier, Chief Product Officer at Veriff. “Liveness tells you a face is real, and while that remains necessary, it is no longer enough. Presence Verification goes beyond the face to analyse signals across the device, the network, full video, and audio, to detect injected deepfakes, scripted bots, and spot the signs that someone is being coached.”
“Customers now have the confidence to reliably identify through audio and video analysis whether onboarding users are being coached by a third party, a capability previously unfeasible without Presence Verification,” said Geo Jolly, Group Product Manager at Veriff. “With an 84% improved detection rate in social engineering fraud sessions, Presence Verification is the critical, front-facing defence layer giving customers peace of mind that genuine users are joining their platforms with authentic action.”
Use cases for Presence Verification
Financial Services & BNPL: Transactions face closer regulatory scrutiny. Confirm the genuine account holder is present before money moves, and detect signs that they are being coached to stop mule accounts or scam-driven loans or transfers. In the UK, authorised push payment (APP) fraud cost £576.4 million in 2025, and payment firms must now reimburse eligible victims up to £85,000 per claim.
Dating: A verified badge only builds trust if the person behind it is real. Check for coached selfies and synthetic faces to ensure matches are who they appear to be.
Marketplace: Verify sellers during onboarding, then step up before payout changes or high-value listings, so buyers and sellers can trust every transaction.
Agentic commerce: As AI agents transact on behalf of consumers, businesses need to check that a real person authorised the purchase. Presence Verification is designed to confirm that the genuine human behind the agent is present at key moments such as account setup or checkout.
Extending trust across the customer journey
Presence Verification is part of a wider set of autumn 2026 updates that enable Veriff to support existing and new customers across marketplaces and financial services:
Unstructured Docs is a fully automated solution that enables organisations to process a wide range of non-identity documents as an essential part of their risk-based procedures, such as confirming a person’s current residential address, bank account, source of income, vehicle ownership, vehicle insurance, and more.
Know Your Business (KYB) expands Veriff’s offering to businesses and the people behind those businesses.
Database Verification extends existing coverage for checking identity, address, and deceased data against authoritative databases to more sources.
Enhancement to Identity Verification to deliver a single unified journey that supports both physical documents and digital IDs; the solution is in private beta.

40% of Kids and Teens Now Turning to AI for Financial Advice
summary:
40% of 6-18 year olds are turning to AI for financial advice, with AI emerging as the second most trusted source for money management, behind only parents (76%) and outranking friends, teachers and social media. New research from GoHenry, the money app helping kids learn to earn, save, spend and invest, also shows that this habit is starting early, with 1 in 4 10-year-olds (25%) asking AI for financial guidance at least once a week.
GoHenry’s Kids’ Eye View of AI research [include link to blog] reveals that this financial curiosity is leading to real-world earnings. Over a third (37%) use AI to help them earn money or pocket money, earning an average of £27.89 per person. Furthermore, 29% are already using AI tools to run side hustles or launch small businesses.
How Young People are Using AI 
When asked how they use AI for money advice specifically, kids and teens pointed to smart shopping (39%), earning money (36%), savings and goals (34%) and money basics (29%) as the top search areas. Additionally, nearly 1 in 5 (19%) have sought AI advice on investing, with boys much more likely to seek AI help in this area (22% vs. 15% for girls). 
As well as financial advice, AI has quickly moved into the everyday routines of young people as they turn to it for help with everything from school work to style advice. The top five overall uses of AI among 6-18 year olds are:
Homework help (69%) - nearly half (47%) use AI for schoolwork at least once a week 
Generating Images & Artwork (61%) 
Social Media Content Creation (53%) 
Smart Shopping, i.e. comparing prices and finding good deals (50%) 
Style Advice (46%)
Parental Pushback and Future Career Anxiety  
While the data reveals that most kids and teens (47%) report positive sentiments like feeling curious, confident, excited, or empowered about AI, over a third (36%) say their parents do not support their use of it, and nearly 1 in 10 (9%) admit their parents have no idea they use it. 
Future job anxiety is also mounting, with over one third (36%) concerned about AI’s impact on their career prospects. When asked what skills would best prepare them to earn a strong income as adults, financial education came first (34%), followed by traditional school subjects like English, Maths and Science (28%). AI came joint third (27%) with coding. 
Bridging the AI Education Gap 
As conversations around education reforms continue, this research reveals a huge demand from 6-18 year olds for modernised, practical education. A massive 73% agree that learning about AI in school would help them better understand the risks and benefits of using digital tools for financial guidance. 
When asked to identify the top AI topics they want taught in school overall, they prioritised the following: 
AI safety, fake news, and deepfakes e.g. learning how to use AI safely and spot fake content (35%)
How to use AI to start a business or make money (32%)
Using AI for creative projects e.g. making music, art, videos, and game graphics (31%)
12-year-old Arran said: “I use AI to check prices before I buy things to make sure I’m getting a good deal and to help me budget. I’m already saving to buy a car when I turn 17 and put down a house deposit after university. I’ve been asking AI about things like Junior ISAs versus normal bank accounts because it helps me understand my options instead of just guessing. It would be good if we were taught how to use it properly at school too." 
Louise Hill, Founder of GoHenry, said: “The growth of AI shows no signs of slowing, so we wanted to give Gen Z and Gen A a voice as it’s their futures that could be impacted the most. Unsurprisingly, many of these young digital natives have embraced AI. However, it’s clear from our research that there is a gap between how kids are using AI, the current education system and their parents’ comfort levels. There is an opportunity here to modernise learning - empowering children and parents alike with the tools to use AI effectively and safely.”

Mastercard Expands Mobile Payment Choice in Morocco With Samsung Pay
summary:
Mastercard is supporting the launch of Samsung Pay in Morocco, expanding consumer choice through secure, convenient mobile payments. Enabled by Mastercard’s tokenization technology, eligible Mastercard cardholders at participating banks can use compatible Samsung devices to make payments, bringing together everyday convenience and built-in payment protection.
The launch builds on Mastercard’s work with financial institutions and technology partners to advance Morocco’s digital payments ecosystem. By extending its capabilities to Samsung Pay, Mastercard is broadening the range of payment options available to consumers and supporting the continued integration of digital payments into everyday commerce.
Samsung Pay builds on Mastercard’s established tokenization capabilities in Morocco. The technology underpinning these payments replaces sensitive card details with a unique digital token, helping protect payment credentials during transactions. Authentication and risk-based safeguards provide additional layers of protection, helping consumers pay conveniently and with confidence.
The launch also reflects Mastercard's global ambition to tokenize 100% of online transactions by 2030. Working with financial institutions and technology partners, Mastercard continues to make digital payments both more secure and simpler to use.
Mohamed Benomar, Country Manager of North West Africa, Mastercard, said, “At Mastercard, we believe the future of payments should give people more choice, greater convenience and confidence in every transaction. Supporting Samsung Pay in Morocco is another important step in expanding access to secure digital payment experiences, underpinned by our tokenization technology: Mastercard Digital Enablement Service (MDES). Beyond introducing another way to pay, our ambition is to make digital payments faster, simpler, and more secure.”
For consumers, Samsung Pay means paying with a compatible Samsung device, with no physical card needed for supported transactions. Participating financial institutions can extend an additional digital payment experience to eligible cardholders, while merchants accepting supported contactless payments can accommodate this additional payment option. Together, these capabilities expand choice across the payment ecosystem.
"With Samsung Pay, we want making a payment to feel as natural as using your smartphone or smartwatch. This launch marks another step in our commitment to providing Galaxy users with innovations that are simple, secure, and genuinely useful in everyday life. We would like to thank participating banks and Mastercard for their trust and collaboration, and we are proud to contribute to this digital transformation," said Hongseok Lee, President of Samsung Electronics Maghreb Arab.
Mastercard and Samsung will also roll out a joint campaign in Morocco to accelerate the everyday adoption of Samsung Pay, combining promotional activity with consumer education on how to pay simply and securely with compatible Samsung devices. The initiative aims to support the long-term growth of digital payments across the country.

Broadridge Brings Proxy Voting to Dinari’s dShares Tokenized U.S. Equities
summary:
Broadridge, a global Fintech leader, and Dinari Inc., a financial infrastructure company enabling the issuance, distribution and trading of tokenized equities, today announced an integration enabling eligible holders of Dinari's dShares™ to exercise shareholder voting rights through Broadridge's established proxy infrastructure.
“Broadridge is bringing trusted governance infrastructure onchain to Dinari’s clients,” said Doug DeSchutter, President of the Investor Communications Solutions business at Broadridge. “We are building the governance layer to support all models of tokenized equities, including Dinari’s custodial model, that preserves the shareholder rights associated with underlying securities. Today’s announcement is the latest step in ensuring investors have access to accurate, institutional-grade governance.”
The integration connects tokenized U.S. equities to the proxy voting processes used in traditional capital markets, allowing eligible dShare holders to exercise voting rights associated with the underlying securities and participate in corporate governance alongside traditional shareholders. These votes are part of the formal shareholder voting process and are counted alongside those cast by traditional shareholders.
“Tokenization should expand how securities are accessed and used without compromising the rights that come with ownership,” said Gabriel Otte, Co-Founder and CEO of Dinari. “Our custodial model was built around that principle. By working with Broadridge, we're enabling dShare holders to participate in actual shareholder votes. This is an important step toward bringing the full functionality of public equities to tokenized markets.”
Dinari’s dShares are structured around a custodial model in which each token corresponds to an underlying U.S. stock or ETF held through established custody arrangements. This structure is designed to preserve the legal and economic rights associated with the underlying securities, including dividends and corporate actions. The integration with Broadridge extends this approach to shareholder governance, enabling eligible dShare holders to exercise voting rights through established proxy voting processes and receive relevant disclosures for the companies in which they invest.
This launch with Dinari builds on Broadridge's onchain proxy voting capabilities, the first platform in the U.S. to support all models of tokenization, including custodial tokenized securities and issuer-sponsored tokens. As the platform evolves, shareholders, including dShare™ holders, will be able to log in and authenticate with their digital wallet to prove their entitlements and vote their proxy ballots directly, bringing the security and accuracy of Broadridge's proxy infrastructure to a native onchain ecosystem.
